{{Short description|Galois group of the separable closure}}
[[File:Complex conjugate picture.svg|right|thumb| The absolute Galois group of the [[real numbers]] is a [[cyclic group]] of order 2 generated by complex conjugation, since <math>\C</math> is the separable closure of <math>\R</math> and <math>[\C:\R]=2</math>.]]

In [[mathematics]], particularly in [[anabelian geometry]] and [[p-adic number|{{math|''p''}}-adic]] geometry, the '''absolute Galois group''' <math>G_K</math> of a [[field (mathematics)|field]] <math>K</math> is the [[Galois group]] of <math>K^\textrm{sep}</math> over <math>K</math>, where <math>K^\textrm{sep}</math> is a [[separable closure]] of <math>K</math>. Alternatively, it is the group of all [[automorphisms]] of the [[algebraic closure]] of <math>K</math> that fix <math>K</math>. The absolute Galois group is well-defined [[up to]] [[inner automorphism]]. It is a [[profinite group]].

When <math>K</math> is a [[perfect field]], <math>K^\textrm{sep}</math> is the same as an [[algebraic closure]] <math>K^\textrm{alg}</math> of <math>K</math>. Notably, this holds when <math>K</math> has [[characteristic zero]] or is [[finite field|finite]].

== Examples ==
* The absolute Galois group of an algebraically closed field is [[Trivial group|trivial]].
* The absolute Galois group of the [[real number]]s is a cyclic group of two elements ([[Complex conjugate|complex conjugation]] and the identity map), since <math>\C</math> is the separable closure of <math>\R</math>, and its [[Degree of a field extension|degree]] over <math>\R</math> is <math>[\C:\R]=2</math>.
* The absolute Galois group of a [[finite field]] <math>K</math> is isomorphic to the group of [[profinite integer]]s
::<math> \hat{\mathbb{Z}} = \varprojlim \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}. </math><ref>{{harvnb|Szamuely|2009}}, p. 14.</ref>
:The [[Frobenius automorphism]] is a canonical (topological) generator of <math>G_K</math>. If <math>K</math> has <math>q</math> elements, the map is given by <math>x\mapsto x^q</math> for all <math>x</math> in <math>K^\textrm{alg}</math>.
* The absolute Galois group of the [[field of rational functions]] with complex coefficients is free (as a profinite group). This result is due to [[Adrien Douady]] and has its origins in [[Riemann's existence theorem]].<ref>{{harvnb|Douady|1964}}</ref>
* More generally, let <math>C</math> be an algebraically closed field and <math>x</math> an indeterminate.  Then the absolute Galois group of <math>C(x)</math> is free of rank equal to the cardinality of <math>C</math>. This result is due to [[David Harbater]] and [[Florian Pop]], and was also proved later by Dan Haran and [[Moshe Jarden]] using algebraic methods.<ref>{{harvnb|Harbater|1995}}</ref><ref>{{harvnb|Pop|1995}}</ref><ref>{{harvnb|Haran|Jarden|2000}}</ref>
* Let <math>K</math> be a [[finite extension]] of the [[p-adic number|{{math|''p''}}-adic numbers]] <math>\Q_p</math>. For <math>p\neq 2</math>, its absolute Galois group is generated by <math>[K:\Q_p]+3</math> elements and has an explicit description by generators and relations. This is a result of Uwe Jannsen and Kay Wingberg.<ref>{{harvnb|Jannsen|Wingberg|1982}}</ref><ref>{{harvnb|Neukirch|Schmidt|Wingberg|2000|loc=theorem 7.5.10}}</ref> Some results are known in the case <math>p=2</math>, but the structure for <math>\Q_2</math> is not known.<ref>{{harvnb|Neukirch|Schmidt|Wingberg|2000|loc=§VII.5}}</ref>
*Another case in which the absolute Galois group has been determined is for the largest [[totally real]] subfield of the field of [[Algebraic number|algebraic numbers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://math.uci.edu/~mfried/paplist-cov/QTotallyReal.pdf |title=qtr |access-date=2019-09-04}}</ref>

== Problems ==

* No direct description is known for the absolute Galois group of the [[rational number]]s. In this case, it follows from [[Belyi's theorem]] that the absolute Galois group has a faithful [[group action|action]] on the ''[[dessins d'enfants]]'' of [[Grothendieck]] (maps on surfaces), enabling us to "see" the Galois theory of [[algebraic number field]]s. It is one of the goals of [[anabelian geometry]] to solve this problem
* Let <math>K</math> be the maximal [[abelian extension]] of the rational numbers. Then '''Shafarevich's conjecture''' asserts that the absolute Galois group of <math>K</math> is a free profinite group.<ref>{{harvnb|Neukirch|Schmidt|Wingberg|2000}}, p. 449.</ref>
*An interesting problem is to settle [[Ján Mináč]] and Nguyên Duy Tân's conjecture about vanishing of <math>n</math>-Massey products for <math> n \geq 3 </math>.<ref name=MT2016>Mináč & Tân (2016) pp.255,284</ref><ref name=HW2023>Harpaz & Wittenberg (2023) pp.1,41</ref>

== Some general results ==
* The [[Neukirch–Uchida theorem]] asserts that every isomorphism of the absolute Galois groups of algebraic number fields arises from a field automorphism. In particular, two absolute Galois groups of number fields are isomorphic if and only if the base fields are isomorphic.
* Every profinite group occurs as a Galois group of some [[Galois extension]],<ref name=FJ12>Fried & Jarden (2008) p.12</ref> but not every profinite group occurs as an absolute Galois group. For example, the [[Real closed field|Artin–Schreier theorem]] asserts that if an absolute Galois group is finite, then it has order 1 or 2.
* Every [[projective profinite group]] can be realized as an absolute Galois group of a [[pseudo algebraically closed field]]. This result is due to [[Alexander Lubotzky]] and [[Lou van den Dries]].<ref name=FJ208>Fried & Jarden (2008) pp.208,545</ref>

==Uses in the geometrization of the local Langlands correspondence==
{{Specific section|date=February 2026}}

In their 2022 paper on the geometrization of the [[local Langlands correspondence]], [[Laurent Fargues]] and [[Peter Scholze]] looked to recover information about a [[local field]] ''E'' via its absolute Galois group, which is isomorphic to the [[étale fundamental group]] of Spec(''E''). This result was calculated while trying to evaluate the [[Weil group]] (which itself is a variant of the absolute Galois group) of ''E''. This result arrives from the idea of the automorphism group ''G''(''E'') of the trivial ''G''-torsor over Spec(''E''); thus, ''G''(''E'') relates to information over Spec(''E''), which is an anabelian question.<ref>{{cite web |title=Fargues, Scholze (2021) |url=https://people.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/scholze/Geometrization.pdf#page7 |ref=15}}</ref>{{primary inline|date=February 2026}}
